observations: The page number «37» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature.

L04-L07 and L13-L16: the two computations, each set as a small table: the words on the left, indented, the equations «= 1», «= 6» in a column on the right; the ditto marks „ of L05, L06, L14 and L15 stand under «für» and, in L05 and L14, under «Jahre», «ist», «die» and «Nota»; L07 and L16, «Summa» and the sum, stand below a short rule under the column. Each printed row is one line here, the cells separated by our «|»; the empty cells give the words room and are not printed. «Ramaḍān» (L06) and «Muḥarram» (L15) are upright in the computations, italic in the text (L03, L09, L11, L17).

L03-L17. Checked: counted from the epoch of the tables, Thursday 15 July 622 (p. 33, JP2 0065), 1 Ramaḍān 529 falls on Friday 14 June 1135 and 1 Muḥarram 520 on Tuesday 26 January 1126, as the examples and the text say; counted from the civil epoch, Friday 16 July 622, both would fall a day later. The notae of the two examples agree with the calendar: Ramaḍān has the nota 6 and Muḥarram 1, and the first eight months have 236 days, five weekdays more than whole weeks; the year 19 has 6 and the year 10 has 1, and the nine years from the beginning of the tenth to that of the nineteenth have 3190 days, also five weekdays more.

L31-L36: the months of the era of Yazdegird in Table 2a. Checked: 16 June 632, the epoch, was a Tuesday (p. 33, JP2 0065), the nota 3 with 1 for Sunday (note 1), and thirty days later a Thursday, 5; 365 days are 52 weeks and a day; the five added days after Ābān make it thirty-five days, five weeks. «Affrordinme», «Azdihestme», «Abenme», «Adarme»: Farvardīn-māh, Ardībihisht-māh, Ābān-māh, Ādhar-māh.

L03: «d. H. ?», the question mark after a thin space (12 px). L26 and L36: «2a», «2b», the letters raised. L20: «Athelhards» spaced; N04: «Al-Bīrūnī», «Sachau» spaced. N05: the closing bracket after «203» is a smaller sort than the other round brackets of the notes, 28 px high where they are 36 px.
The colons and semicolons stand after the thin space of the edition (8-12 px measured).
